messages:
alex: Heads-up: proposing a migration plan for switching quota/dashboard attribution from `legacy_route` -> `route_hint` canonical field. This thread is to sync on mapping job, reconciliation, SDK helpers, and console saved-filter compatibility. Short TL;DR: run mapping job, dual-write for 48h, flip read keys, reconcile.

mika: sounds good. main concern is double-billing windows and dashboard spikes. Do we have a safe atomic switch?

alex: plan is not atomic. We do: 1) import known legacy->route_hint mappings into new bucket keys, 2) enable dual-write (write to both keys) for 48h, 3) run reconciliation job that compares sums and flags deltas, 4) schedule a short freeze to switch reads to route_hint only. Freeze < 5m.

jordan: dual-write implies increased write QPS on counters. Ops: can infra handle extra load for peak?

ops-bot: infra note: counters are sharded; we can provision +25% shard capacity for rollout window. Please open infra Jira for shard bump.

mika: also need to ensure quota reset semantics align. If a counter moves to a new key, resets should not double-apply.

alex: right. Migration will copy current value and set an anchor timestamp. The reconciliation job will treat anchor as "migrated" so resets after anchor only affect new bucket. Edge-case: rapid consume between copy and dual-write start. We'll accept tiny window and flag any tenant with >0.5% drift.

sasha: console saved filters: many orgs use strings like `preview:beta` in dashboards. We'll build a compatibility index: when parsing filter strings we map `preview:.*` -> `policy=preview;team=$1`. We'll also add a compatibility tag `legacy_route_preview` to old events for 30 days.

jordan: for SDKs, we should provide a helper to generate canonical route_hint from common shorthands so customers can migrate client-side. I'll add helpers for TS and Go. Example helper API: `RouteHint.fromPreview('beta-team')` returns `policy=preview;team=beta-team`.

devex: can you also ship a CLI that scans a project's usage of preview headers and outputs a migration report? That will help customers before upgrading.

jordan: yes, I'll add `rdw-migrate-scan` in npm and a small go binary. Basic usage: `rdw-migrate-scan --dir . --out report.json`

mika: streaming client note: retries may reuse header cache. Need to ensure header value is consistent across reconnects and included in metadata events. Otherwise attribution will be partial.

alex: good catch. For Python we will update the streaming layer to stash route_hint on the connection object and include it for reconnects and reconnect attempts. Also emit it in the lightweight per-request metadata since full traces are sampled.

sasha: telemetry merging: console relies on request_id to join sampled traces and metadata rows. Are we certain request_id persists across retries and redirects?

ops-bot: request_id is assigned at ingress and propagated downstream via `X-Rdwd-ReqID`. Retries on client side generate new reqIDs; server maps retries to original via an `idempotency_key` if provided. We should recommend clients set an idempotency header for critical flows to allow grouping.

alex: recommendation: include `X-Rdwd-Idempotency-Key` from SDKs for retryable requests. Update SDKs to set it by default for non-fire-and-forget calls.

jordan: small SDK patch plan: 1) add `RouteHint` type + builder, 2) inject header key `X-Rdwd-RouteHint` when feature flag `sdk_route_hint_v2` enabled, 3) fallback to `X-Rdwd-RoutePreview` if not. Also add `idempotency` defaulting behavior for streaming/long-poll endpoints.

mika: tests: we need unit for header fallback, e2e that verifies metadata event contains `route_hint`, and an integration that runs migration job on staging and compares counters. I'll own the integration tests.

sasha: console: will add migration UI showing customers which saved filters will change, with diff preview and a one-click migrate button. That UI needs backend endpoints that accept a mapping table.

alex: mapping table will be stored in config repo as key-value pairs and versioned. We'll publish table v1 with common mappings (preview variants, legacy tokens). Teams can propose additions.

jordan: about normalization: some clients send underscores, some hyphens. Are we canonicalizing? Server should.

alex: yes server-side normalization: convert `_` -> `-` in `policy` token and lower-case all tokens. We'll keep a whitelist for known policy values to prevent creating high-cardinality tags. Unknown tokens map to `policy=other`.

mika: index concerns: console tag index caps out at 100k unique values. We must guard against arbitrary free-form team ids in route_hint. How to prevent customers from injecting high-cardinality keys?

sasha: plan: only index a curated subset of tokens (policy, cost_center, region). Other tokens are stored in raw metadata but not indexed. We'll surface a warning in the console if customers attempt to include non-indexed tokens.

alex: rollout timeline proposal: week 1: mapping job + staging parser + SDK canary; week 2: opt-in dual-write in production for internal orgs; week 3: public SDK canary + reconciliation; week 5: flip reads and deprecate legacy header.

jordan: +1. We should also prepare a rollback plan: if reconciliation shows >1% drift for top 50 tenants, pause and revert reads.

mika: agree. Add telemetry dashboards to monitor drift and spikes (top N by delta).

sasha: action items: I will prototype saved-filter migration UI and compatibility banner. Jordan: prepare SDK helper + CLI. Mika: create integration tests and migration job script. Alex: finalise mapping table and rollout doc. Ops: open infra ticket for shard capacity bump.

ops-bot: Jira created: RDW-1245 (shard bump for route_hint migration).

devex: I'll draft migration guide + sample scripts and publish link in rollout doc.

alex: thanks everyone. Please drop a one-line +1 or call out any blocking risk by EOD. If no objections we'll lock the plan and schedule the canary.
